exactPrompts.references/second-identity-front.png: A single straight-on orthographic character reference for a realistic historical game: a fictional 31-year-old Irish-born New York seamstress in 1896. BALD head for mesh construction, bare neck and the tops of shoulders only. Slim elongated oval face, narrow jaw, prominent straight nose with a slightly broad tip, thin naturally shaped lips held closed, light grey-green eyes, auburn eyebrows, fair ruddy skin with restrained freckles, subtly tired lower eyelids. Thoughtful, calm neutral expression, no smile, no frown. Strongly distinct from a broad-cheeked middle-aged Mediterranean shopkeeper. Authentic adult anatomy, natural asymmetry and skin detail. Neither beauty photography nor glamour. Face exactly forward, eyes level and looking straight ahead, ears visible, lips together, symmetrical framing. Entire skull visible with generous margin; no hair, no hat, no jewelry, no clothing, no makeup. Flat evenly lit neutral grey background, soft frontal diffuse light, minimal shadow and no dramatic highlights. Production-quality realistic game character reference, no text, no labels, no collage.
exactPrompts.references/hair-strands.png: A seamless repeating PBR BASE COLOR texture tile of fine natural human hair strands, viewed very close and perfectly flat. Hair is very dark chestnut brown with about twenty percent fine silver-grey strands, suitable for a sober 46-year-old woman's neatly combed 1896 low bun hairstyle. Dense parallel strands run VERTICALLY from the top edge to bottom edge. Delicate naturally varying strand width and color; convincingly photographic fine detail, NOT a painted illustration. Soft brown-grey color variation, subtle tiny flyaway fibers, zero black gaps, full coverage. Even diffuse light, NO baked directional highlights or shadows, NO glossy white stripe. Seamless left-to-right and top-to-bottom. This is a square texture only: no head, no face, no hairstyle silhouette, no scalp, no border, no text.

historicalUncertainty: The dress and hairstyles use period examples as art references, not a documented outfit or coiffure of a particular Sicilian immigrant shopkeeper. The supplied fashion plate directs the side coverage but its exact date is unverified. University of Louisville item ULPA 1980_020_0971 is catalogued to 1889–1899; the ca. 1895 Carlotta Maury profile is another reference. No historical photograph or fashion-plate pixels are in the game textures.
limitations: Appearance recipes from two head bases are not separately authored personalities. Strong feature combinations require visual review.
Speech is a timed procedural pattern, not audio-synchronised phonemes.
The seated skirt uses an authored carrier, not cloth simulation.
Hair uses shaped opaque masses with alpha-masked fine strands; it has no strand simulation.
rejectedExperiment: The MPFB canonical-head fit did not preserve likeness or lid quality. Its comparison source is retained as a rejected study and is not used by the game or normal rebuild.

prompts.references/hair-fibres-v2.prompt.txt:
Tool: built-in image_gen, 2026-10-30
Output: hair-fibres-v2.png

Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless PBR base-colour texture for realistic game hair. Generate one square 2048 by 2048 macro texture tile, completely filled edge to edge by dense, naturally irregular fine human hair fibres, all running vertically top to bottom. Natural medium-dark warm brown hair. Several hundred very fine individual strands with varied widths, subtle individual brown values, tiny natural deviations and soft smaller groupings. The material should look like actual fine combed human hair under perfectly even diffuse flat cross-polarised illumination. This will be UV mapped around sculpted 1890s waved updos, so do NOT draw an actual hairstyle, face, head, curl silhouette, scalp, braid, background or objects. NO glossy bright stripe, NO directional studio highlights, NO painted broad grooves, NO wood grain, NO thick locks, NO text, NO borders. Seamless tiling on all four edges, consistent average colour across the whole image, all hair parallel and fully opaque. This is the albedo only: all lighting and highlights will be supplied by the renderer.

The returned asset is 1254 by 1254 pixels. The normal map is derived at 512
pixels; the strand coverage map is project-authored at 1024 pixels. No
historical photograph or user-supplied fashion illustration is in the maps.
prompts.references/hair-curls-v1.prompt.txt:
Tool: built-in image_gen, 2026-10-30
Output: hair-curls-v1.png

Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: tileable PBR albedo texture for the sculpted mass of a realistic late nineteenth-century woman's curly updo in a game. A square macro photograph filled edge to edge with dense natural dark warm brown wavy-curly human hair. About eight to twelve loose S-shaped and softly coiled locks across the width, each made of many extremely fine individual fibres. The coils overlap irregularly into a coherent mass of natural hair; subtle brown variations and fine flyaway hairs. Soft waves with some tighter small curls, not dreadlocks, not tubes, not a woven pattern. This is the diffuse base-colour texture only: flat even cross-polarised illumination, restrained soft occlusion between locks, no glossy bright stripes or dramatic highlights, no shadows from external objects. Seamless on all four edges. No head, scalp, face, hat, body, props, background, labels, border or text. Natural slightly imperfect strands, photographic surface detail. Keep overall dark-brown value consistent across the tile. This texture will wrap around curved 3D hair clumps and will be tinted to different hair colours.

The returned asset is 1254 by 1254 pixels. The normal map is derived at 512
pixels. No historical photograph or user-supplied fashion illustration is
included in the maps.
